sector_model: Satellite telecom with a pending acquisition: OEBITDA, leverage, subscribers, government revenue and deal terms; not a generic screen.
thesis: Iridium (Nasdaq: IRDM) is being acquired by Rocket Lab for 27.00 cash plus 0.4000 RKLB shares when the RKLB 10-day VWAP is at or below 67.50 (collar to 112.50; DEFM14A filed 2026-08-26), expected to close mid-2027. At the 2026-11-16 closes (IRDM 45.03, RKLB 57.37) the consideration is about 49.95 per share, a 10.9% gross spread, but the stock leg falls one for one with RKLB below 67.50 (RKLB fell 10.5% in four sessions). Q3 2026: revenue 245.7M +8%, service revenue 187.5M +13% (Aireon closed 2026-07-02), subscribers 2,696K +6%, OEBITDA 135.6M -1%, net income 106.9M including a 103.9M Aireon gain. TTM revenue 903.0M, NI 163.0M, FCF 277.6M (capex PP&E only) = 5.8% yield on 4,780M market cap; 9M buybacks zero versus 186.5M in 9M25. Net debt 2,061.6M, 4.2x TTM OEBITDA. Dividend 0.15 rising to 0.16. This is a merger-arbitrage and Rocket Lab stock-risk situation, not a standalone value idea.
counterthesis: The spread exists because the deal can fail or RKLB can fall: Iridium owes a 223.6M termination fee in some cases, closing needs HSR, FCC and other approvals with an end date of 2027-06-28 extendable to 2027-12-28, and Rocket Lab funds cash through a 3.6B bridge, debt or equity, with no financing condition. Standalone, leverage is 4.2x with a 5.0x covenant at Aireon and 183.4M seller debt due about July 2027; OEBITDA fell in Q3; GAAP earnings are inflated by the gain. Government revenue is about 29% of 9M sales and the EMSS contract extension runs only to March 2027.
invalidation: Thesis fails if regulators block the deal and IRDM reverts to a standalone leveraged multiple, if RKLB falls further so consideration drops well below the current price, or if OEBITDA turns down on lost government revenue.
